I wrote the report to `/home/user/workflow-foundry/research/review-20261007/10-STATE.md`, about 380 lines. Landing this work makes Foundry's measurements honest and its engine cheaper, but it does not move any capability claim. There is one narrow positive result and one small result that leans negative. Nothing has been measured on sealed, real-world or owner-written tasks.

**What landing does and doesn't cover.** Measurements are at HEAD `0aaa6d5`. Two snapshot commits landed while I was writing: `d28403a` (Kev wave A part 2) and `37e53e1`, which includes an early copy of this report.
- **Not in HEAD yet:** the work-conserving scheduler (`src/runtime.mjs:459-461` still runs nodes in batches) and `foundry cancel`/stop-all. The report assumes both land.
- **Still open for the engine freeze (E1) after landing:** the sink-field label policy, the reviewed sandbox launcher, the usage-limit pause, viewer fields G1–G3 and executor isolation. By my count about 5.75 of the 10 planned engine items are done once the scheduler and cancel land.
- **No `STAGE1-ENGINE.md` exists.**

**Main findings, recomputed from source files:**
- **Every workflow built so far fails the new lint.** That is 5 of 5, including the hand-written P1 workflow (11 errors). Under the new verdict rules the 32 C0 Foundry trials go from 32 `pass` (5 of them wrong) to 32 `unverified`: no false passes, but no true passes either.
- **Costs before and after are not comparable.** The CLI flags cut a trivial Haiku 5.5 call by 41–42% and its median time from 2.99 s to 1.53 s (n = 10 per arm).
- **Fan-out is no longer a bottleneck.** A 1,000-item map now takes 15–16 s and about 2.9 CPU-seconds on the new store (my scratch benchmark), against 73–135 s of pure overhead before.
- **Auto-heal ran live tonight.** Across three campaigns up to 21:52 UTC, 20 defect fixes were proposed by Haiku, Sonnet and Opus. The code checks refused 19 and the 20th ran out of budget, so none was promoted. Only two mechanical "add the missing gate" patches were promoted. All incidents are on already-inspected seeds, so this proves the plumbing, not a fix rate. The campaign was still running, so its numbers may change.
- **Test suites:** main suite 912 tests, 894 pass, 0 fail, 18 skipped. Kev data factory 341 tests, 340 pass, 1 skipped (the only test that runs the real model). Run viewer 91 of 91 pass.
- **Kev:** stock Kev ties or loses to the rule baseline on 4 of 5 decision types; injection 0.64 vs 0.99, failure-class 0.69 vs 1.00. `03-probe-results.md` is still a placeholder.
- **Laptop throughput:** the document's "1,000–1,300 tokens/s" holds at 300 and 2K tokens but is about 770 at 8K.
- **Docs disagree:** README L66/L86 and THESIS D13 say Kev laptop training waits for the Kev-vs-Haiku comparison; README L337 says it is approved and starts. README also still says stage-1 "has not landed" and lists 220 agent-framework items (it is 217).

**Overall position:** 45 of 120 depth points (38%). Only 2 of 20 layers have a baseline comparison on held-out tasks, and 0 have sealed, real-world or owner-task evidence. If the six-week plan lands on schedule, about 68 of 120. The engine work is a little over half way to the first claim-bearing round. Depth measures how far the evidence goes, not whether it is good, and every new point can come back negative.

The report also covers:
- nine strategic risks, including cheaper one-shot models catching up, construction cost not paying back, evaluation validity, executor security without a credential, and "honest but blind" verdicts;
- what each upcoming experiment's result would change in the plan;
- my own odds on the five deciding questions, marked as guesses.

**Top 10 gaps, ranked by importance to the vision**
1. **No sealed, real-world or owner-task number.** Everything is development evidence on Claude-written families with burned seeds. R-bench has 0 runs, the sealed families are unused, no owner tasks have arrived and no external benchmark has run.
2. **No oracle discovery, so "honest" means `unverified`.** There is no success signal for heal, router labels, reuse or the UI that isn't a model's opinion.
3. **Haiku as builder is unshown and leans negative** (11/16, one build per cell). The structured builder and typed templates don't exist.
4. **No router or slider, and nothing has measured whether there is anything to route.** The evidence so far often says "no workflow" is the right size.
5. **"Any workflow" is declared, never compiled or executed.** No `call`, triggers, error branches, tool loop or media.
6. **Executor security blocks subagents and agentic workflows.** There is no network isolation, and 48% of agent-framework items need a tool loop.
7. **Heal and edit have no fix rate** (0 of 20 defect fixes promoted on inspected incidents).
8. **Reuse and learning are unbuilt**, and the premise that tasks recur is unmeasured. A build pays back after 3–10 successes, or never.
9. **Composition at scale is untested:** no `call`, `wide`, best-of-K baseline, board or AMP combinations.
10. **Kev is unproven against Haiku 5.5.** Nothing is trained, the probe write-up is a placeholder, and the docs contradict each other on training.

**Headline.** After landing, the critical path is:

1. Engine freeze E1, target 10-16.
2. Haiku structured builder with oracle discovery, 10-23 (likely 10-28). This is the longest pole: about 13–23 engineer-days, never built.
3. CX3, structured vs free Haiku builder, 10-30 (likely 11-06).
4. C0 sealed round, read once, 11-08 (likely 11-15). This is the first claim-bearing number.
5. First end-to-end run on the owner's tasks, 11-22 (likely 11-29).

The rest of the maximalist vision (call, executors, swarm, board, reuse, AMP, the composed run) follows from mid-November to February, each behind its own experiment and kill rule.

- **Depth projection [I]:** 45/120 now, about 67 by 11-22, about 78 by end-January. No layer reaches depth 6 without the owner's recurring-task list (decision 11).
- **Spend [I]:** experiment calls are about $620–1,740 through 11-22 and $1.7–4.0K through January. R-bench harness building adds $1.3–1.8K of agent time. The upper ends pass the $1,500 soft cap, so the owner needs to set a spending cap (D1-cap) by 11-01, before the sealed round.

**Changes from the earlier six-week plan (synthesis §5):**
- **E1 earlier:** moved from 10-27 to about 10-16, because most of the engine work landed on 10-08.
- **Oracle-discovery metric:** oracle discovery gets its own metric, OD1: the share of bad controls and mutants the built acceptance rejects.

- **Slider check moved:** RX4 moves from the C0 sealed round to the R-bench sealed 40, since no router can be frozen before 11-02.

- **Budgets re-estimated:** EX1 is $60–200, not $15–30, which only covered the three development incidents. CX3 is $60–120 with the Haiku 4.5 arm.
- **Executor question narrowed:** a no-credential route exists only for a Foundry-owned capped tool loop. The B1 script arm already runs with no network and model access only through a host gateway socket (`experiments/lib/arms/b1-script.mjs`, `src/executors/sandboxed-command.mjs`) [M]. I wrote `/home/user/workflow-foundry/research/review-20261007/11-CRITIQUE-ambition.md` (886 lines). It holds 5 P0, 11 P1 and 8 P2 findings, each with evidence and an exact change to 10-STATE or 11-NEXT. No other file was written and git state was not touched. Every claim is tagged measured (with its path), documented or inferred.

**Main findings, P0:**
1. **Interactive, visual and game work (ROADMAP claim C5) is missing from both documents, for the second time.**
   - 10-STATE's rubric has no layer for it and 11-NEXT has no milestone.
   - `src/ports.mjs` has no env port.
   - The synthesis had restored it as a "first slot after 11-24" defer row; 11-NEXT dropped that row.
   - As a result `sealed-3` is never read, and M17's board experiment depends on `gridquest`, which cannot run without the env port.
   - ROADMAP Tier A beds and the τ^τ-bench feasibility gate are also gone.
   - Fix: add a milestone for the env port and image inputs (M13-ENV), a C5 pilot, and rubric rows 21 and 22.
2. **The composed system is integrated last: February 2027 at the earliest.**
   - Much of composition can be tried on the current frozen engine: nesting by inlining, `wide` built from `map`, and a board as state carried round by round.
   - ROADMAP (lines 892–893) only requires a named frozen engine per comparison, so these experiments need not wait for the sealed round.
   - Fix: a vertical-slice end-to-end run (M24), composition-by-emulation arms merged into M16 (M25), and named experiment freezes (E1x).
3. **The slider's "how big" half is never measured.** RX1 tests only "direct vs workflow", using lint-invalid legacy artifacts, yet its kill rule can remove the whole router. Fix: limit the kill to the need axis and add RX1b for template / construct / construct+.
4. **Oracle discovery sits inside the longest task (M2).** Fix: split it out so OD1 is measured at $0 by 10-14, and add acceptance elicitation (asking the task owner for examples) so owner tasks with no oracle can reach `pass`.
5. **R-bench building waits on run 1 for no reason.** Building items 6–30 takes about two days and does not depend on any experiment's result. Fix: 30-item run 2 around 11-15 and the sealed-40 read around 12-06, instead of December and late January.

**Main P1 findings:**
- Auto-heal cannot "make what's missing": its 13 patch operations cannot add a step, tool or sub-workflow.
  - New data since 10-STATE: run 4 refused 4 more proposals, so it is now 0 fixes from 24 defect proposals across Haiku, Sonnet and Opus.
  - The H-p1 incident does not reproduce: 8/8 retries passed on both the original and the healed workflow.
  - Fix: add structural patch operations, and make the builder's repair step reuse the heal engine.
- "Edit" is only ever measured as repair; added EX2 for directed edits.
- Learning has no experiment, and reuse needlessly waits for `call`.
- The executor default is the narrowest option (c), although a capped tool loop needs no new credential; propose (a).
- The schedule is costed in engineer-days, but measured throughput on 10-08 suggests review capacity is the real limit.
- The concurrency caps override the owner's "Full speed" choice.
- Haiku-vs-Opus-skeleton credit is never separated in "Haiku constructs" results.
- Kev's K1 gate compares stock Kev, which can stop training before any fine-tune runs.
- A 7–9B open-model probe on the laptop is proposed (one evening, $0 API; needs the owner's OK).
- EX1 claims to use CX3's failures but runs before CX3.
- The AMP "parallel workflows" ask is measured only as an AMP-context A/B.

**Cost and decisions:**
- **Added spend:** about $135–305 through 11-22 and $315–725 through January, list price, estimated.
- **Projected effect:** evidence depth on the original 20 layers rises from 78/120 to about 84/120 by end of January.
- **D1-cap** has to move earlier, to 10-19.
- **Five owner decisions are listed in §6:**
  - building R-bench items 6–30 now;
  - executor route (a);
  - D1-cap moved to 10-19;
  - the open-model probe;
  - confirming that "Full speed" applies to experiment slots.

Two things to know: 10-STATE.md was being edited by another agent while I read it, and the heal campaign was still writing to its ledger ($5.09 by 22:15 UTC), so those numbers may move.

I wrote the critique to `/home/user/workflow-foundry/research/review-20261007/11-CRITIQUE-rigor.md`; no other file was touched and git state was not changed. The arithmetic in 10-STATE and 11-NEXT mostly holds; the main problems are in the plan's design. Four figures are wrong or out of date: the RX1 run time, the sealed-round cost, the heal results and the money spent so far.

**What I re-ran:**
- The P1 and C0 analysis scripts reproduce every number both documents quote.
- The engine suite on the current working tree gives 919 tests, 901 pass, 0 fail, 18 skipped (10-STATE had 912/894 at HEAD).
- The run-view tests pass 91/91.
- Recounts of the corpus, Kev probe ledgers, lint audit, CLI-flag study, R-bench harness cost and all heal runs through 22:18 UTC.
- The Kev data-factory suite (about 25 minutes) was not re-run.

**P0, fix before the plan goes to the owner or the engine freeze (E1) is named:**
1. **The 300 s per-call timeout is still the default.** It is at `src/models/port.mjs:114` and `claude-cli.mjs:97`; `b0-call.mjs` does not override it, and the runner still counts a timeout as a task failure. P1 called the resulting single-call gap "largely a harness artefact", yet the RX1 router pilot, R-bench run 1, the E1 re-check and the sealed round all inherit it. 11-NEXT never mentions timeouts.
2. **The sealed round, read once, cannot decide what it is for.**
